# mutation-53 — stain

## Primitive

A **stain** is a machine visa leaked by production argument worlds. Default is the CI gate: `--check --bound` only, empty stdout when production leaked no machine, exit 1 with the leaked *machine* (worlds as evidence). Tests are a projection (`--emit`), not the object.

## Why this might not exist

`admit` fused hatch's due world to visa's skip and printed a test file. `--check --bound` was the honest "production leaked no machine" signal — and still dumped a pytest stub on a clean tree:

```
# generated by admit — production worlds; skip unless the visa holds
from __future__ import annotations
import pytest

# no generable due fixtures
```

sitbone and kizu are bound-empty. CI that runs `admit --check --bound` gets 149 bytes of a module nobody asked to compile. Concatenation is `hatch | visa`; the leftover generator banner is `admit` used as a linter.

Discarded as a flag on admit: `--check --bound` already existed. The default *was* the generator. A CI binary whose silent 0 means "no host in production" is a different verb.

## How to run

```bash
chmod +x ./stain
./stain --self-test
./demo.sh
./stain -C fixtures/ugly
./stain -C ~/ghq/github.com/annenpolka/sitbone
./stain --emit -C fixtures/ugly isBrowser
./stain --due -q -C ~/ghq/github.com/annenpolka/sitbone isBrowser
```

Python 3.10+, stdlib. Exit 0 on clean (or successful `--emit`). Exit 1 on machine-tied debt. `--due` fails on OPEN worlds too. No test file unless `--emit`.

## Empirical transcript

### v0.1 — default is the check; sitbone/kizu empty

`./stain --self-test` ok. `./demo.sh` → **passed=102 failed=0**.

ugly (Alice HOME in production, Brave OPEN in the same Swift file):

```
./stain -C fixtures/ugly
# load_profile  skipif  BOUND  MISS  HOME=/Users/alice USER=alice platform=Darwin
#   load_profile("/Users/alice")
#   src/profile.py:12
# load_profile  skipif  BOUND  MISS  HOME=/Users/alice USER=alice platform=Darwin
#   load_profile("/Users/alice/Library")
#   src/profile.py:13
# loadHome  skipif  BOUND  MISS  HOME=/Users/alice USER=alice platform=Darwin
#   loadHome("/Users/alice/Library/sitbone")
#   src/App.swift:32
# exit 1
# no import pytest, no XCTest, no Brave, no GitHub title
```

`--summary` on ugly: `machines=1  bound=3  due=22  open=17  spec=2`. Three worlds, one Alice. Default stdout still repeated the visa three times.

This host's HOME MATCH is still a stain (CI does not care the laptop holds the visa). `--emit` of that world PASSes here.

Textbook `/home/user` and GitHub titles: default empty, exit 0.

sitbone (read-only, 2026-08-20):

```
./stain -C sitbone          # exit 0, stdout empty
--summary                  machines=0 bound=0 due=80 assert=10 skip=70 open=80
--due -q isBrowser         exit 1   (six OPEN members are still due)
--emit isBrowser           6 OPEN XCTAssertTrue, overlay 6/6 pass, no skip
```

kizu: `machines=0 bound=0 due=332 skip=281 open=332`, default empty exit 0. Neither tree's production callers leaked a HOME.

### v0.2 — a stain is the machine, not the fixture

ugly's census already said `machines=1`. Default stdout still listed Alice three times, once per due world. CI does not care how many callers recorded `/Users/alice`; it cares that production leaked that host.

After: group default (and `--due` bound subset) by require set. Worlds become evidence.

```
./stain -C fixtures/ugly
# stain  machines=1  worlds=3  miss=1
#   MISS  BOUND  HOME=/Users/alice USER=alice platform=Darwin
#     load_profile  load_profile("/Users/alice")  src/profile.py:12
#     load_profile  load_profile("/Users/alice/Library")  src/profile.py:13
#     loadHome  loadHome("/Users/alice/Library/sitbone")  src/App.swift:32
```

`HOME=/Users/alice` prints once. Porcelain stays per-world (parseable). sitbone/kizu still empty. Live `$HOME` MATCH is still `machines=1` (CI still fails). `./demo.sh` → **passed=105 failed=0**. Overlay still 6/6.

## Dogfood targets

- `fixtures/ugly` — Alice home, textbook quote, GitHub title, macOS comment beside Brave
- this host's live `$HOME` (MATCH stain) vs `/Users/alice` (MISS stain)
- sitbone / kizu `--bound` empty

## Surprises

- sitbone needed no skip: production never recorded a machine. The joint is still visible — default empty is the new green, while `--due` stays 1 because six browser members (and 70 dyn skips) are still due.
- MATCH this-host HOME is a CI fail. admit's emitted test would PASS on this laptop; stain fails because the leak exists.
- ugly's three Alice worlds were already `machines=1` in the census. v0.1 stdout still repeated the visa; v0.2 made the census grain the default object.

## Failures

- `runAppleScript` is a private instance method. `--emit` recovers the Safari script; the test still cannot construct `self`.
- `--due` on a whole sitbone tree is noisy (70 dyn skips). Bound is the useful grain; that is why it is the default.
- JS/TS options-bag worlds stay coarse (hatch's).

## Suggested mutations

- `--held`-style: when did a production world newly acquire a visa?
- Construct `Type()` / use existing fixtures when the subject is an instance method.
- Join with alibi: splice `--emit` tests onto old production (LOCKED-and-BOUND vs LOCKED-and-OPEN).
- `--allow HOME=/Users/alice` documented exceptions so a recording fixture can exist on purpose.

## Kill / keep

**Keep.** The object is not admit-with-`--check`. sitbone/kizu default empty is the CI product admit still wrapped in a pytest stub. v0.2 makes the leaked *machine* the report grain (ugly: 1 stain, 3 worlds). Kill only if a later generation proves `admit --check --bound >/dev/null` is the same verb — it is not, because the generator remains the default and the stub still leaks.
